title: Articulated ants after the lateral tuck fix
question: Do these read as animals rather than chains, and does a tucked body squeezing through a gap read as squeezing?
context_md:
Two of the colony's four founded ants (seed=1, scene=colony, world frame 3600 = noon), walking on the bank surface. Report of record: Reports/creature-articulated-body-2026-09-09.md §7f.

Before this fix a lateral's own collision could block the whole body's step -- measured 43.9%/96.8% blocked on flat/rolling terrain, against a plain 6-cell chain's 2.5%/12.4%. The rule now: a widened segment's lateral takes its authored side if placeable, else the other side, else it tucks (not placed that step) and re-emerges automatically once room returns.

ascii's colony-forage round-trip count is back at 32 (was 0, bar is >=6, pre-articulated-body baseline was 23).
